reviews.review: WH40K: Space Marine is freaking awesome. I played through it on my Steam Deck on Hard, it looked and ran great. The game looks a LOT like Gears of War but it is much more action-oriented, with no cover system and a focus on mowing down waves on enemies. It plays great and is a ton of fun. Now, keep in mind it is pretty short (around 8 hours) and I wish it had more variety. It is also disappointing that [spoiler]there is a giant mech you do not control[/spoiler]. Overall though it is a blast. The story is also surprisingly good for a game in this genre (and also, it must be said, it is structured similarly to the original Gears). I can say without a doubt I have never felt more like a space marine than I did in this game, highly recommended. I just wish the multiplayer was still alive because I want to keep playing it!

I really, really want to like this game. The intensity, the style, the weight in playing is fantastic. I finished it back in the day on PS3. However, I hate it.

The gameplay, a mix of third person shooting and melee with a bonus health component, encourages forward movement even into masses of enemies. It's thrilling to push forward blindly, risking it all to cross swords with a host of orks. However, you have a surprisingly small health pool, making pushing forward extremely risky. In order to offset this, Space Marine gives you the ability to setup oks for a special attack that gives you back health.

I find the health-regenerating attack to be extremely finicky and annoying to try and pull off. Add in suicide enemies and all the orks that carry ranged weapons (rifles and explosives), and there is suddenly a very high chance you'll be killed before the attack even finishes. This is because the health-regenerating attack forces you to sit through an animation that is way longer than it needs to be.

If it was easier to see approaching threats and setup a defense, all this might be more tolerable. However, even back when I first finished this game, I hated the level design. I never quite know from what direction I'll be attacked, or the number of enemies I'll face. Very often, I would try and pick my moment to charge in with a melee weapon, as this is the most exciting part of the game for me, and I would be instantly overwhelmed by a dozen additional enemies from a direction I wasn't watching. The only way I could make progress without dying the first time I entered any encounter was to play super lame and sit back with only a gun.

Space Marine is very much not a cover shooter. The weapons are loud and fun, but I found myself bored with them over time because the melee aspect was so much more of a thrill the few times it went right.

Space Marine is a disappointing slog to me. Maybe you'll understand the level design better, or you're one of those gamers who is happy to die over and over, or maybe you're just a super action game or Warhammer 40k fan. The game might be for you. It's not for me.
